findingDetails.title: The 006 kind-list row catches the plan kind order but not its kind count, so the plan OpenBot six kinds stands against a reference type that declares seven
findingDetails.scopeProof: The row is research.md:206; the plan claim is B/006-approval-grants/spec.md:99 and its six-kind list is REQ-002 at :160; the reference type is C/OpenBot-main/app/src/lib/approvals.ts:62-69; the doc row that merges the two kinds is C/OpenBot-main/docs/approvals.md:41, all read directly.
findingDetails.case: A builder fixes the order as the row says, keeps six kinds, and a security-settings change is classified credentials; the plan action-kind.ts then reports a kind set OpenBot does not have, and no test covers a security_settings question.
findingDetails.claim: The row checks the kind order and never says the plan has six kinds where the reference type declares seven.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read the whole differences row and the 006 section for a mention of security_settings or a seven-kind count; neither appears.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The plan deliberately merges credentials and security_settings because approvals.md:41 covers both in one row, so the count difference is a design choice rather than an error.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: A line in the 006 section that says the plan merges the reference two credential kinds into one.

results.summary: Every security-relevant row checked resolves to a line that says what the row claims; one row checks the kind order and misses the kind count
